subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Apr 2024 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured priorities correctly and to outline next steps:

High-level pain points you shared
- "Noisy tenants" cause spikes that blow past our shared capacity and lead to degraded latency for other customers.
- Current proxy-based solution is brittle and requires manual rule changes per incident.
- Lack of per-customer routing and tiering means we can’t offer differentiated SLAs or pricing.

Current stack you described
- Fronted by Kong + custom throttling middleware.
- Redis for short-term counters; Kafka for async events.
- ML features currently hosted on a mix of managed GPU instances and an internal inference service (no tenant-aware routing).

Success criteria for an evaluation
- Ability to enforce per-tenant rate limits and quotas (burst + sustained) with <100ms added p95 latency.
- Configurable routing policies per-customer (route high-tier customers to reserved capacity, fallback to shared).
- Metrics and audit logs per-tenant for billing and compliance (30/90/365d retention options).
- Easy admin UX for creating tiers, policies, and emergency overrides.

What we (Redwood) can offer / relevant features
- Tenant-aware routing rules that can map requests to dedicated pools or shared GPU pools based on tenant ID or API key.
- Fine-grained rate limits and quota enforcement (token-bucket) with burst and sustained windows; enforcement at the ingress layer to protect workload isolation.
- Policy-based tiering to pin customers to dedicated capacity or to give priority during contention.
- Per-tenant observability: token-level cost breakdown, latency heatmaps, and audit logs export (S3/Drive).

Open questions from our side
1) How do tenants authenticate today? API key, JWT with tenant claim, or some other header?
2) Typical token/request rate per-customer (p95) and what you consider a noisy tenant threshold.
3) Any compliance constraints for logs (encryption, restricted access)?

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive with your infra/plat team (suggested: Tue Apr 9, 10–11am PT). Stephanie (cc’d) will run through a short demo of tenant routing and quota config.
- Share PoC proposal and SOC2 summary (attached).
- If procurement is needed, loop in your procurement contact so we can align on timelines and contracts.

Attachments: poc-proposal-acme.pdf (scope + timings), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, multi-tenant-arch.png

If anything above is off, please flag and I’ll update. Thanks — enjoyed the discussion and excited to partner on this.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Apr 2024 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications / priorities from my side:

Priorities
- Top priority: per-customer rate limits that prevent noisy tenants from impacting others. We need emergency override controls for SRE during incidents.
- Second: routing by tier so our "Enterprise" tenants hit reserved capacity (we’re comfortable with slightly higher cost for guaranteed latency).
- Third: per-tenant billing metrics (daily export to our billing pipeline).

Answers to your open questions
1) Auth: We use API keys scoped to tenant IDs (rotated monthly). We can surface a tenant-id header for routing if needed.
2) Typical: p95 requests per minute for medium tenants = ~120 rpm; noisy tenant threshold we’re concerned about starts at ~2k rpm sustained.
3) Logs: must be encrypted at rest, and access restricted to a small set of accounts (SOC2 controls). Retention 90 days for audit, 365 days for billing exports.

Procurement contact: procurement@acmeretail.com — they’re cc'd here and will help with any timelines/contract questions.

We are available for the tech deep-dive Tue Apr 9, 10–11am PT. Please send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acmeretail.com | +1 206-555-9012
